 Judgment

These appeals are filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity), calling in question the judgment and award dated 05.08.2017, passed in M.V.C.No.3928/2016, on the file of the VII Additional Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal &
XXXII, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity).

Motor Accident Claims Tribunal &
XXXII, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru

sentences.text: MFA No.1102/2018 is filed by the insurance company questioning the liability, as well as the quantum of compensation awarded.
MFA 6573/2018 is filed by the claimant for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

Brief facts:
2. On 20.10.2014, at about 1.30 p.m., the claimant was going on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-42-J-4906, on Harohalli-Kanakapura Main Road, in front of Pandurangaswamy Temple, Kanakapura town at that time one Tata Sumo bearing No.KA-05-C-2134, came in a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed Shri. Prakash vs Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73940377/
3 against the claimant's motor cycle.

entities.text: Prakash vs Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd

sentences.text: Due to the said impact, the claimant was thrown on the road and sustained severe injuries to his left hand and left leg.

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimant under Section-166 of the M.V.
Act, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.99,510/-, along with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.

The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 therein,
liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
REGARDING LIABILITY:
5.

In the present case, the offending vehicle Tata Sumo bearing No.KA-05-C-2134,
which is a Light Motor Vehicle (Transport).
The Driver was holding a driving license to drive LMV (Non-Transport), as per Exhibit-R2.
On this ground, the insurance company had filed an appeal seeking to exoneration of the liability.
The issue involved is no longer res-integra.

In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1, the driver who is holding a driving license to drive LMV (Non- Transport) is also competent to drive LMV (Transport).

entities.text: MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Just because there is no endorsement in the Driving License of Transport that cannot be said that the Driver is incompetent to drive LMV (Transport).
Therefore, as per the principle of law laid down in the above stated case, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

(2017) 14 SCC 663 REGARDING QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
6.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
 Pain and Suffering : Rs. 30,000/-
 Loss of income during laid up : Rs. 13,000/-
 period

Medical bills : Rs. 9,070/-
 Loss of Future Earning : Rs. 37,440/-
 Loss of Amenities, conveyance, : Rs. 10,000/-
 food and nourishment, attendant  charges etc.
 TOTAL : Rs. 99,510/-

sentences.text:
As per the Wound Certificate at Exhibit-P6, Discharge Summary at Exhibit-P8, and the documentary evidence, it is proved that the claimant had suffered the following injuries:
"Tenderness over left shoulder, Terminal restriction of movements of left shoulder by 10% in all directions when compared to the right side movements are painful terminally, Loss of strength of left shoulder muscles by 20% when compared to the right side, X-ray shows midly mal-united fracture of left greater tuberosity of humerus, United fracture of left distal phalanx of 5th raw of foot."
8.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'Pain and Sufferings at Rs.30,000/- is appropriate and hence kept intact.
7. The claimant was aged 34 years and the accident has occurred during the year 2014.
The claimant was working as Cook.

The Tribunal has held the income of the claimant at Rs.6,500/- per month,
which is on lesser side.
Therefore, as per Chart of notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, a sum of Rs.8,500/- is to be taken as notional monthly income of the claimant.
The Doctor has assessed 3.22% permanent physical disability to the whole-body.
The criteria for calculating functional disability is elaborately discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another2.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, considering the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court stated supra, 3% functional disability to the whole-body as assessed by the Doctor is taken.
The appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others. Vs. Delhi Transport Corpn And Another3 is '16'.

entities.text: Smt.Sarla Verma & Others. Vs. Delhi Transport Corpn And Another3 is '16'
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss of Earning Capacity Due to Disability' is recalculated and quantified as follows:
Rs.8,500 x 3% x 16 x 12 = Rs.48,960/-
8.

The compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal under the 'Medical Expenses'
at Rs.9,070/- is per actual bills and receipts and the same is kept intact.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation towards 'Loss Of Amenities, Food, Nourishment,
Conveyance and Attendant Charges' at Rs.10,000/-, which is on lower side and hence a sum of Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the said head.
10.
In view of the accidental injuries, the claimant would have taken rest for atleast for a period of TWO months.

Therefore, by taking income at Rs.8,500/- per month and calculating the laid up period for TWO months, the claimant is entitled for a sum of Rs.17,000/- (Rs.8,500 x 2 months),
under the head 'Loss Of Earning During Laid Up Period'.

Therefore, in modification of the award of the Tribunal, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:

 Loss of income during laid up : Rs. 17,000/-
 period (8500 x 2 months)
 Medical bills : Rs. 9,070/-
 Loss of Future Earning : Rs. 48,960/-
 (Rs.8500 x 3% x 16 x 12)
 Loss of Amenities, conveyance, : Rs. 30,000/-
 food and nourishment, attendant  charges etc.
 TOTAL : Rs. 1,35,000/-
REGARDING INTEREST :
14. The Tribunal has awarded interest at 8% per annum, but the same is scaled down to 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
Therefore, to this extent, the appeal filed by the insurance company is liable to be allowed.
15. Therefore, the appellant-claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,35,000/- as against Rs.99,510/-.

The appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.35,490/-
(Rs.1,35,000 - - 12 - Rs.99,510) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization,
in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of total compensation within Eight Weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.

16. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. MFA No.1102/2018 filed by the insurance company is allowed in part.
